title: Noomo | The power of digital Storytelling
text:
The power
of digital
storytelling

In a world that’s

constantly shifting,


what

guides

us through

change,

reinvention,

and the unknown–


Stories emerge
through


The best stories

don’t just

speak to

us.
They

invite us inside.


Storytelling is much
more than words.

It is how a spark

becomes a fire.


Storytelling is what you

see, feel, hear, interactwith.

is narrative.


Light

Spirit

Sound

How can the story live at the
heart of the experience?

Start with clarity
Know what you’re trying to say.
Whether it’s launching a product or
building emotional connections,
the goal needs to be clear.

Let the story guide design
Every animation, interaction,
and visual should serve the
narrative. If it doesn’t help
tell the story, it’s not needed.

Experiment and iterate
Some of the best ideas came from
simply trying things out, seeing
what clicked, and refining from
there.

Make it personal
The best stories create emotional
connections. Whether through AI
personalization or custom design
elements, find ways to make the
experience unique for each user.

Where stories
become experiences

Reimagine Phoenix

Let us help you tell your story the way it was meant

Resn Customer Privacy Notice

This privacy notice tells you what to expect us to do with your personal information.

What information we collect, use, and why

We collect or use the following information for service updates, marketing purposes and to comply with legal requirements:

Names and contact details
Marketing preferences
Location data
IP addresses
Website and app user journey information
Records of consent, where appropriate
LAWFUL BASES
PART 1

Our lawful bases for collecting or using personal information for service updates or marketing purposes are:

Legitimate Interest

The provision and management of worldwide support services (e.g., IT) for our business activities. Enhancing our Site and Services, creating trend analyses and benchmark reports, and comparable objectives. Managing customer relations and enhancing our Sites and Services, encompassing additional marketing and analytical activities. Detection and prevention of fraudulent activities, encompassing misuse of Services or money laundering. Safeguarding physical, IT, and network perimeter security. Conducting internal inquiries and investigations.

LAWFUL BASES
PART 2

Our lawful bases for collecting or using personal information for legal requirements are:

Legitimate Interest

We reserve the right to disclose information pursuant to subpoenas, court orders, and other lawful requests from regulators and law enforcement agencies, including those necessitated by national security or law enforcement disclosure obligations. Such disclosures are founded upon our legitimate interests and/or compliance with applicable laws.

Safeguarding our legal rights and preventing misuse: to safeguard the integrity of the sites and our business operations; to prevent and identify fraud, unauthorized activities and access, and other forms of misuse; where deemed essential to investigate, prevent, or undertake measures in response to unlawful activities, suspected fraud, circumstances involving potential threats to the safety or legal rights of individuals or third parties, or breaches of our Terms of Use or this Privacy Policy.

WHERE WE GET PERSONAL
INFORMATION FROM
People directly
Third parties: We collect information from third-party sources including social networks, platform providers, payment processors, and operators of specific third-party services utilized by us.
HOW LONG WE KEEP
INFORMATION

In accordance with standard practices, we retain your personal information for the duration necessary to achieve the purposes for which it was collected, or as required to comply with our legal obligations, resolve disputes, maintain accurate business records, and enforce our contractual agreements. Typically, we retain pertinent personal information of clients and site visitors for a minimum of three years following our last interaction with you, and in alignment with our obligations under applicable laws. We may retain personal information for extended periods as mandated by our regulatory responsibilities, professional indemnity obligations, or where we believe it is necessary to establish, defend, or safeguard our legal rights and interests, or those of others.

WHO WE SHARE
INFORMATION WITH

Data Processors — Google Analytics

This data processor does the following activities for us: We employ Google Analytics to assess the use of our services and platforms, to enable us to collect non-personal information about users, and to enhance our Services and user experiences.

Other Organizations

Organisations we need to share information with for safeguarding reasons
Professional or legal advisors
Financial or fraud investigation authorities
Relevant regulatory authorities
External auditors or inspectors
Warranty and guarantee providers
Organisations we're legally obliged to share personal information with
Emergency services (where necessary)
Other relevant third parties: The data processor may use cookies and other technologies and may aggregate the information gathered about you on our sites with other data collected for their own purposes
YOUR DATA
PROTECTION RIGHTS

Under data protection law, you have rights including:

Your right of access
You have the right to ask us for copies of your personal data.

Your right to rectification
You have the right to ask us to rectify personal data you think is inaccurate. You also have the right to ask us to complete information you think is incomplete.

Your right to erasure You have the right to ask us to erase your personal data in certain circumstances.


Your right to restriction of processing
You have the right to ask us to restrict the processing of your personal data in certain circumstances.

Your right to object to processing
You have the right to object to the processing of your personal data in certain circumstances.

Your right to data portability
You have the right to ask that we transfer the personal data you gave us to another organisation, or to you, in certain circumstances.

Your right to withdraw consent
When we use consent as our lawful basis you have the right to withdraw your consent.

You don't usually need to pay a fee to exercise your rights. If you make a request, we have one calendar month to respond to you.

To make a data protection rights request, please contact us using the contact details at the top of this privacy notice.

SECURITY MEASURES

We have instituted safeguards and technical measures to safeguard the personal information within our control against unauthorized access, use, or disclosure. Nonetheless, it is important to note that no data security measures can ensure absolute security.

DIRECT MARKETING

You have the right to opt out of receiving direct marketing emails from us by following the instructions provided in such emails or by contacting us via email at hello@resn.co.nz. Please note that we may still send you transactional or service-related communications, including service announcements and administrative messages.

INFORMATION
REGARDING MINORS

The Resn website is designed for individuals aged 16 and above. We do not intentionally or specifically gather information about minors under the age of 16. If you suspect that we have inadvertently collected such information, please inform us at hello@resn.co.nz, so we can remove this information from our servers.

AMENDMENTS TO
OUR PRIVACY POLICY

Periodically, we may revise this Policy to incorporate new or modified privacy practices or to adhere to shifts in industry standards or legal mandates. When significant modifications are made to this Policy, we will publish a notice online. Furthermore, if these changes substantially impact the manner in which we utilize or disclose information, we will provide advance notification by posting a notice on our site. We urge you to periodically review this Policy for the most current information regarding our privacy practices.

HOW TO COMPLAIN

If you have any concerns about our use of your personal data, you can make a complaint to us using the contact details at the top of this privacy notice.

If you remain unhappy with how we've used your data after raising a complaint with us, you can also complain to the relevant authority.

United States
Federal Trade Commission (FTC)

Address: Federal Trade Commission, Consumer Response Center, 600 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW, Washington, DC 20580
